title: Annotatio IV §.XIX: Lucawitz — true bread in nature; body sacramentally, really, SPIRITUALLY
pass_a_gloss: In the First Part Johannes Lucawitz, chief doctor of the Taborites, against Rokycana and the Prague Papists, thus confesses concerning the Sacrament of Christ’s Body and Blood: Concerning this Sacrament, he says, we hold this from the faith of scripture and sincerely believe in the heart, that the bread which Christ taking in His Supper gave His disciples to eat, and in its worthy perception through the Ministry of faithful priests left as a memory of His passion, is in its nature true bread, which by the pronoun This is pointed out in this sacramental proposition: This is my body, and with this the true body of Christ taken from the Virgin and handed over for us — not identically, not understanding material identity, but sacramentally, really and truly — which on account of its habitude toward Christ’s body is to be held in due reverence, and the faithful venerate it not as it is bread’s substance, but insofar as, as premised, it is Christ’s body, whose true body is to be believed to be in the same truly, sacramentally, SPIRITUALLY. Not however with all essential and accidental properties following it.
pass_b_english: Lucawitz (chief Taborite doctor): the Supper bread is in its nature true bread — the ‘This’ of ‘This is my body’ points to that bread.

With it is Christ’s true body from the Virgin — not material identity, but sacramentally, really, and SPIRITUALLY; reverence for the habitude to Christ’s body, not for bread’s substance as such; not with all essential/accidental properties.
source_text: Parte Primâ Johannes Lucawitz, Taboritarum præcipuus doctor, contra Rokenzanam & Papistas Pragenses, ita de Sacramento Corporis & Sanguinis Christi confitetur: De hoc, ait, Sacramento, istud ex fide scripturæ tenemus & corde sinceriter credimus, quod panis quem Christus in sua Cœna accipiens, suis ad manducandum dedit discipulis, & in ejus digna perceptione per Ministerium fidelium sacerdotum reliquit memoriam suæ passionis, est in natura sua verus panis, qui pronomine, Hoc, demonstratur in hac propositione sacramentali: Hoc est corpus meum, & cum hoc verum corpus Christi de Virgine sumtum & pro nobis traditum, non identicè, non de identitate materiali intelligendo, sed sacramentaliter, realiter & verè, qui propter sui habitudinem ad corpus Christi, in sibi debita habendus est reverentia, & fideles illam venerantur non ut est panis substantia, sed de quanto, ut præmittitur, est corpus Christi, cujus verum corpus in eodem esse veraciter, sacramentaliter, SPIRITUALITER, est credendum. Non autem cum omnibus proprietatibus tam essentialibus quam accidentalibus consequentibus ipsum.
